title: Gratitude
subtitle: A Thanksgiving source sheet: from Adam's ingratitude to Leah's thanks, and why gratitude has to flow through us
intro: Rashi says the builders of Babel were "children of Adam" because they inherited his ingratitude. Leah is the first person in history to thank God, and she does it in the middle of heartbreak. The Hebrew word for thanks also means "I confess." These sources trace hakarat ha-tov, recognizing the good, from Genesis to the Pilgrims' turkey.

sections.title: The First Ingrate
sections.blurb: The Torah's first sin after the fruit is a failure to say thank you.

sources.author: Bereshit
sources.he: וַיֵּרֶד יְהוָה לִרְאֹת אֶת־הָעִיר וְאֶת־הַמִּגְדָּל אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ בְּנֵי הָאָדָם׃
sources.en: The LORD came down to look at the city and tower that the children of man had built.

sources.author: Rashi
sources.he: בְּנֵי הָאָדָם. אֶלָּא בְּנֵי מִי? שֶׁמָּא בְּנֵי חֲמוֹרִים וּגְמַלִּים? אֶלָּא בְּנֵי אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁכָּפָה אֶת הַטּוֹבָה וְאָמַר "הָאִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּה עִמָּדִי", אַף אֵלּוּ כָּפוּ בַּטּוֹבָה לִמְרֹד בְּמִי שֶׁהִשְׁפִּיעָם טוֹבָה וּמִלְּטָם מִן הַמַּבּוּל.
sources.en: THE CHILDREN OF MAN (ADAM): Whose children could they have been? Perhaps the children of donkeys or camels? Rather, it means the children of Adam Harishon, who proved himself ungrateful when he said, "The woman whom You gave to be with me" (Gen. 3:12). These people, too, were ungrateful, rebelling against the One who had showered kindness upon them and rescued them from the Flood (Genesis Rabbah 38:9).

sources.author: Rashi
sources.he: אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּה עִמָּדִי. כָּאן כָּפַר בַּטּוֹבָה (עבודה זרה ה:).
sources.en: WHOM YOU GAVE TO BE WITH ME: Here he showed his ingratitude (Avodah Zarah 5b).

sources.author: Rashi
sources.he: כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר. וּמַה טַּעַם לֹא הִמְטִיר? לְפִי שֶׁאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, וְאֵין מַכִּיר בְּטוֹבָתָם שֶׁל גְּשָׁמִים. וּכְשֶׁבָּא אָדָם וְיָדַע שֶׁהֵם צֹרֶךְ לָעוֹלָם, הִתְפַּלֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם וְיָרְדוּ, וְצָמְחוּ הָאִילָנוֹת וְהַדְּשָׁאִים.
sources.en: FOR IT HAD NOT RAINED: Why had God not sent rain? Because there was no human being to work the soil, and no one to recognize the goodness of rain. When Adam came and understood that rain is a necessity for the world, he prayed for it, and it fell, and the trees and grasses sprouted.
sources.note: The world's first rain waited for someone who would notice it.

sources.author: R. Shai Held
sources.en:
Commenting on Pharaoh's purported ignorance of Joseph, a midrash asks, "But how can this be, for to this very day, the Egyptians know the kindness Joseph did for them?!" Rather, the midrash answers, "Pharaoh knew Joseph but did not pay him adequate attention, and was ungrateful to him. And in the end, he was ungrateful to God as well, as it says, 'I do not know the Lord.' From this we learn that ingratitude is closely related to rejection of God" (Midrash Ha-Gadol to Exod. 1:8)...

If we are ungrateful, if we don't acknowledge the reality of just how much has been given to us rather than made or achieved by us, we will actually be incapable of worshipping anything but ourselves. It is not surprising, then, that the prophet Ezekiel imagines Pharaoh insolently declaring, "The Nile is mine; I made it for myself" (Ezek. 29:3).

sources.author: Louis Feldman
sources.en: Connected with the quality of philanthropia is the virtue of showing gratitude. Thus we find that Josephus, in an extra-Biblical addition (2.42), states that Joseph refused the overtures of Potiphar's wife not merely because of the immorality of her request but also because it would be an outrage to the host who had honored him so highly. Indeed, ironically, when Potiphar's wife accuses Joseph to her husband, she charges him with ingratitude in that he had forgotten the benefits which he had received from Potiphar.

sources.author: Denis Diderot
sources.en: Gratitude is a burden, and every burden is made to be shrugged off.

sections.title: Gifts No One Earned
sections.blurb: Why gratitude starts with noticing that existence itself is a gift.

sources.author: Maimonides
sources.en: Loving-kindness is practised in two ways: first, we show kindness to those who have no claim whatever upon us; secondly, we are kind to those to whom it is due, in a greater measure than is due to them. In the inspired writings the term hesed occurs mostly in the sense of showing kindness to those who have no claim to it whatever. For this reason the term hesed is employed to express the good bestowed upon us by God... On this account, the very act of the creation is an act of God's loving-kindness. "I have said, The Universe is built up in loving-kindness" (Ps. 89:3).

sources.author: Tehillim
sources.en: How can I repay the LORD for all His bounties to me?

sources.author: Sefer HaChinuch
sources.he: משרשי מצוה זו, שראוי לו לאדם שיכיר ויגמל חסד למי שעשה עמו טובה, ולא יהיה נבל ומתנכר וכפוי טובה, שזו מדה רעה ומאוסה בתכלית לפני אלקים ואנשים. ושיתן אל לבו כי האב והאם הם סבת היותו בעולם, ועל כן באמת ראוי לו לעשות להם כל כבוד וכל תועלת שיוכל, כי הם הביאוהו לעולם, גם יגעו בו כמה יגיעות בקטנתו. וכשיקבע זאת המדה בנפשו, יעלה ממנה להכיר טובת האל ברוך הוא, שהוא סבתו וסבת כל אבותיו עד אדם הראשון, ושהוציאו לאויר העולם וספק צרכו כל ימיו, והעמידו על מתכנתו ושלמות אבריו, ונתן בו נפש יודעת ומשכלת, שאלולי הנפש שחננו האל יהיה כסוס כפרד אין הבין, ויעריך במחשבתו כמה וכמה ראוי להזהר בעבודתו ברוך הוא.
sources.en: From the roots of this commandment [honoring parents] is that it is fitting for a person to acknowledge and return kindness to those who were good to him, and not to be a scoundrel, a stranger and an ingrate, for that is a bad trait, utterly repulsive before God and people. He should take to heart that his father and mother are the cause of his being in the world, and so it is truly fitting to give them every honor and every benefit he can, for they brought him into the world and labored over him when he was small. Once he fixes this trait in his soul, he will rise from it to recognize the good of God, blessed be He, who is his cause and the cause of all his ancestors back to the first man; who brought him out into the world's air and supplied his needs all his days, made his body whole and upright, and gave him a mind that knows and reasons, for without the mind God granted him he would be "like a horse, like a mule, without understanding." And he should weigh in his thoughts how very fitting it is to be careful in the service of the Blessed One.
sources.note: Gratitude is a ladder: parents first, then God.

sources.ref: Seder Eliyahu Rabbah ch. 15 (14), ed. Friedmann p. 69
sources.author: Seder Eliyahu Rabbah
sources.en: He who denies himself a good life in this world is an ingrate, showing contempt for the King's bounties and grace.

sources.ref: Sapphire from the Land of Israel
sources.author: Rav Kook (R. Chanan Morrison)
sources.en: Our food (and in the case of the farmer, also his livelihood) is supplied by cows, chickens, and so on. We should feed these animals first as an expression of the fundamental gratitude we should feel toward these creatures which provide us with our basic needs.

sources.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
sources.en: Cultivate the habit of being grateful for every good thing that comes to you, and to give thanks continuously. And because all things have contributed to your advancement, you should include all things in your gratitude.

sections.title: Leah: Grateful and Disappointed
sections.blurb: The first person to thank God did it from inside a heartbreak.

sources.author: Bereshit
sources.he: וַתַּהַר עוֹד וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתֹּאמֶר הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת־יְהוָה עַל־כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ יְהוּדָה וַתַּעֲמֹד מִלֶּדֶת׃
sources.en: She conceived again and bore a son, and declared, "This time I will thank the LORD." Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

sources.author: Talmud Bavli
sources.he: מיום שברא הקדוש ברוך הוא את עולמו לא היה אדם שהודה להקדוש ברוך הוא, עד שבאתה לאה והודתו, שנאמר: "הפעם אודה את ה׳".
sources.en: From the day the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world, no one thanked the Holy One, blessed be He, until Leah came and thanked Him, as it is said: "This time I will thank the LORD."

sources.author: R. Shai Held
sources.en: It is one thing to be grateful when everything is wonderful, when all our dreams have been fulfilled and all our hungers sated. But it is quite another to be grateful when life is complicated, when some of our most cherished dreams have remained painfully unrealized, when some of our yearnings are so intense that they threaten to burn right through us. Leah is the first person to feel and express gratitude even and especially amid profound sorrow and enduring disappointment.

sources.author: R. Norman Lamm
sources.en: Judah was named Yehudah by his mother Leah ("ha-pa'am odeh et Hashem"), because of her gratitude to the Lord. Then, "va-yaker Yehudah," from today's Sidra we learn of Judah rising to the quality of vidui, the acknowledgment of guilt. Finally, in next week's sidra Jacob gives him sovereignty in the words "Yehudah atah yodukha ahekha," recognition of his leadership. All three — gratitude, confession, and recognition — are implicit in the name Yehudah, or in the Hebrew word hodaah.
sources.note: The root y-d-h: thanks, confession, and acknowledgment are one word.

sections.title: Modeh: Thanks as Confession
sections.blurb: The first words a Jew says each morning are an admission of dependence.

sources.author: R. Norman Lamm
sources.en: Basically, gratitude to G-d means acknowledging our dependence upon Him. We CONFESS our need of Him, our inability to get along without Him. No wonder that in Hebrew the word for thanks — MODEH — also means: I confess! I confess my need of You, I thank You for coming to my assistance! The Modeh prayer we recite upon arising each morning means not only "thank You, G-d" for returning my soul to me; it means also, "I confess, O G-d," that without you I would never wake up alive!

sources.author: R. Norman Lamm
sources.en: Indeed, gratitude is one of the greatest principles of Judaism. The first thing the Jew says upon arising in the morning is: Modeh ani, thank you, O God, for returning my soul and my life to me. And when, a thousand years ago, the great Gaon Saadia wanted to show that it is possible to construct Judaism de novo on entirely rational grounds, the very first principle that he produced was: gratitude, from which flow the commandments of prayer, of saying grace after food, of charity, and so on.

sources.author: Gal Gadot
sources.en: I say thank you every morning. In the Jewish culture, there's a prayer that you're supposed to say every time you wake up in the morning to thank God for, you know, keeping you alive... You say 'modeh ani,' which means 'I give thanks.' So every morning I wake up and step out of bed and I say, 'Thank you for everything, thank you, thank you, thank you, thank you.' Nothing is to be taken for granted.

sources.author: Marcus Aurelius
sources.en: When you arise in the morning think of what a privilege it is to be alive, to think, to enjoy, to love...

sources.author: Tehillim
sources.he: אוֹדְךָ עַל כִּי נוֹרָאוֹת נִפְלֵיתִי נִפְלָאִים מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וְנַפְשִׁי יֹדַעַת מְאֹד׃
sources.en: I thank You, for I am awesomely, wondrously made; Your work is wonderful, and my soul knows it well.

sources.author: R. David Kirshenbaum, citing R. Shlomo of Radomsk
sources.he: אַז די עטליכע ווערטער פון יתרו? — איז דער תירוץ: יתרו האָט עפּעס מחדש געווען. די אידען האָבען געזאָגט שירה און געדאַנקט השי"ת פאַר די טובות און חסדים וואָס ער האָט געטאָן צו זיי; אָבער דאַנקען השי"ת פאַר דעם גוטס וואָס ער האָט געטאָן אַ צווייטען איז געווען אַ נייעס, און יתרו איז געווען דער ערשטער דאָס צו טאָן.
sources.en: Why are Jethro's few words ["Blessed is the LORD who rescued you"] so celebrated? The answer: Jethro innovated something. The Jews sang the Song at the Sea and thanked God for the kindness He had done for them. But thanking God for the good He did for someone else was new, and Jethro was the first to do it.

sections.title: Feeding Gratitude
sections.blurb: Resentment grows on its own. Gratitude needs reminders, practice, and a table.

sources.author: Dennis Prager
sources.en: The servant did not only make a request of God; he also offered a prayer of gratitude once his request had been granted. Prayers expressing gratitude are among the highest levels of prayer. Anyone can petition God (or people). The finest individuals are those who express gratitude after their request is fulfilled. It is almost impossible to overstate the power of gratitude. It is the root of both goodness and happiness. Ungrateful people cannot be either good or happy; indeed, such people are likely to be both bad and unhappy.

sources.author: Dennis Prager
sources.en: This is the only time God told a patriarch to build an altar. All other times, the patriarchs spontaneously built one. Perhaps God wanted Jacob to have a physical reminder of His intervention on Jacob's behalf "when you were fleeing from your brother Esau." Gratitude must be constantly fed (unlike resentment, which lives on naturally), and physical reminders are essential. The Torah is filled with commandments consisting of physical reminders — e.g., eating unleavened bread (matzah) for the seven days of Passover... and building booths on the Festival of Booths.

sources.author: Dennis Prager
sources.en: Jacob spoke of God in personal terms, focusing on what God had done for him. Gratitude is powerful, as it is the mother of both goodness and happiness. Neither is possible without gratitude... But a word of caution is appropriate here. The view of God as provider can lead to problems — to regarding God as a sort of "celestial butler," a heavenly being whose purpose is to provide for us whenever we need something... If God's primary role is to do things for us, what happens when He doesn't? People may stop believing in Him. If the Provider stops providing, maybe there is no Provider.

sources.author: Torah commentary
sources.he: וה׳ ברך את אברהם בכל — ופשוטו שאברהם הרגיש ברכה בכל אשר לו. דלפעמים יש לאדם רכוש לרוב ואין בזה ברכה, שאין לו מנוחת הנפש והוא תמיד משתוקק ליותר. אבל אברהם נתברך בכל אשר לו, שהרגיש ברכת ה׳ ברכושו, ולא היה חסר לו מאומה. ובדרך זו ביאר השל"ה הקדוש "ודורשי ה׳ לא יחסרו כל טוב" — לא נאמר שיש להם כל טוב, שעל זה לא הובטחו כלל, אלא לא יחסר להם כל טוב, היינו שמתברכים בברכת ה׳ שלא ירגישו במחסור.
sources.en: "And God blessed Abraham with everything" (24:1). The plain meaning is that Abraham felt blessed in everything he had. Sometimes a person has wealth in abundance and there is no blessing in it: he has no peace of mind and always craves more. But Abraham was blessed in all he had: he felt God's blessing in his possessions and lacked nothing. In this way the holy Shelah explained "those who seek the LORD shall not lack any good" (Ps. 34:11). It does not say they will have every good thing, which was never promised, but that they will not lack: they are blessed with God's blessing so that they do not feel want.

sources.ref: The Meaning of God in Modern Jewish Religion, p. 227
sources.author: R. Mordecai Kaplan
sources.en: "In the millennium," say the Rabbis, "all other sacrifices will be abolished, but the thank-offering will not be abolished; all other prayers will be abolished, but not the prayer of thanksgiving." The Rabbis could conceive of a situation in which all propitiatory prayer and sacrifice would become superfluous and meaningless, but the spirit of grateful appreciation is of the essence of religion, and can never be dispensed with. It represents the highest aspiration of the human soul for experiencing the goodness or godliness of life.

sources.ref: Being Good: Jewish Ethics for Daily Life
sources.author: R. Joseph Telushkin
sources.en: There are proven techniques for becoming a happier person, and one of them is becoming a more grateful person.

sources.ref: Practice Gratitude; Greater Good Science Center
sources.author: Nice News
sources.en: Studies suggest that gratitude can help you sleep, eat, and feel better, and that the simple act of writing down three things you're thankful for each day can improve your health. But while it's easy to acknowledge the advantages, we don't always take the time to build the habit, especially when we're experiencing negative emotions.
sources.note: See "How Gratitude Changes You and Your Brain" (greatergood.berkeley.edu).

sections.title: Through Us, Not Merely To Us
sections.blurb: Real gratitude spills over: into sharing, repaying, and setting the table for others.

sources.author: R. Shai Held
sources.en: I'd like to propose another (perhaps complementary) way of thinking about why the thankful person needs to invite others to share in his or her meal: The nature of gratitude is such that it is inherently outward looking... The simple requirement that there not be any leftovers from the thanksgiving offering thus teaches us a fundamental theological and spiritual lesson. We are not meant to rest content with being recipients of God's gifts but are asked to become givers ourselves. God's gifts are meant to flow through us and not merely to us.
sources.note: The todah had to be eaten in a day and a night: too much food for one family, so you had to invite people.

sources.author: R. Shai Held
sources.en: Gratitude as a posture is enormously important for me to teach and to talk about, because as I understand it in Judaism, gratitude is always bound up with a desire to repay. I've been given so much, how can I repay it... Do the gifts of God flow through me or do I try to grab them and hoard them?

sources.author: R. Norman Lamm
sources.en: We conclude with the words of David, Hodu la-Shem ki tov, ki le'olam chasdo. Usually this is translated, "Give thanks unto the Lord for He is good, for His love lasts forever." I would paraphrase that, in a manner that is consistent with the syntax of the Hebrew verse: "Give thanks to the Lord, for it is good," i.e. it is good for the heart and soul of the thankful person to be grateful, "for His love is over all the world." Wherever man seeks, no matter how desolate the landscape of his experience and environment, he will find evidence of the great goodness of Almighty G-d.

sources.author: Springwise
sources.en: A blockchain app that lets coffee drinkers trace their beans back to the farm that grew them, and send the farmer a thank-you.
sources.note: Rav Kook's "feed the animals first," updated for the supply chain.

sources.author: R. Gedalia Dov Schwartz
sources.en: Jews of America ought to be grateful to the Pilgrims for having celebrated the first Thanksgiving with the turkey, a clean bird, instead of using for their festive occasion an unclean animal or fowl which would have caused so many of our brethren to violate Kashruth.
sources.note: Hakarat ha-tov, all the way down to the menu.

questions: Rashi reads Babel as an inheritance of Adam's ingratitude. Why would ingratitude lead to tower-building?
Leah thanks God while still unloved. Is gratitude amid disappointment more or less sincere than gratitude when things are good?
If modeh means both "I thank" and "I admit," what are you admitting when you say thank you?
Prager says gratitude must be fed and resentment lives on its own. What are your physical reminders?
The todah could not have leftovers. Who is at your table this year who would not otherwise be?
